title: Cellular immune function in chronic renal failure depending on the extent of proteinuria
summary:
People with chronic kidney disease are at high risk of developing infections. Therefore, signs of infection must be responded to very quickly; in severe cases, an antibiotic must be prescribed more quickly than in people with healthy kidneys. Vaccination measures are advisable; in some cases their effectiveness should be checked by blood tests.
With regard to precautionary measures in the event of infections, people are currently considered to have chronic kidney disease if the eGFR value, a measure of the detoxification function of the kidneys, has fallen below 45 ml/min. In some kidney disease patients, however, the disease is not primarily expressed in the eGFR value, but rather there is predominantly increased protein excretion in the urine. It is not yet known whether these people are equally affected by the risk of infection and should be protected.

In a clinical study, three groups of people are now to be examined for immune defense characteristics:
1) Kidney patients with an eGFR below 45 ml/min
2) Kidney patients with an eGFR above 60ml/min but abnormal urine protein excretion
3) Individuals with normal kidney function as a comparison group

interventions.name: Proteinuria: uACR > 300 mg/g creatinine AND eGFR > 45 ml/min 1,73m2
CKD: eGFR ≤ 30 ml/min 1,73m2 independent of proteinuria
Control: eGFR > 60ml/min 1,73m2 AND uACR < 30 mg/g creatinine

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Determination of eGFR from serum creatinine and urine ACR on the day of recruitment
- Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Need for renal replacement therapy
- Presence of a functional kidney transplant
- Treatment with any immunosuppressive medication within the last 4 weeks
- Treatment with rituximab, obinutuzumab, or cyclophosphamide within the last 12 months
- Infections at the time of the study or within 2 weeks before the study
- Child-Pugh stage C liver cirrhosis
- Active malignancy with or without specific oncological therapy
- Blood transfusion within 4 weeks before inclusion, severe anemia with current indication for blood transfusion
- Presence of pregnancy
- Lack of consent to participate in the study
- Inability to understand study procedures and provide valid informed consent
- Persons who are housed in an institution by court or official order
- Simultaneous participation in an interventional study
